definition: MongoDB Basics is a core concept in MERN Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What MongoDB Basics is
theory.body: MongoDB Basics describes the methods and patterns used within MERN Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: MongoDB Basics is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why MongoDB Basics matters
theory.body: Without MongoDB Basics, systems built with MERN Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How MongoDB Basics works
theory.body: The mechanism behind MongoDB Basics follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of MongoDB Basics.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of MongoDB Basics
theory.body: MongoDB Basics offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
